This method renders the background environment for rays that have transmitted through the volume by sampling a layered spherical map [S1, unofficial].

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly describes a rendering loop for the background. It initializes a `ConcentricSpheresIntersector`, calculates steps based on `grid.background_nlayers`, and iterates through radii. Inside the loop, it normalizes the ray position to the unit sphere (`ray.pos *= invr_mid`), converts it to equirectangular coordinates (`_unitvec2equirect`), and calculates a layer index based on `grid.background_nlayers`. It then performs trilinear interpolation (`trilerp_bg_one`) on `grid.background_data` using these coordinates and layer indices. Finally, it accumulates color based on optical depth (`sigma`) and adds a final transmission term multiplied by `opt.background_brightness`. This process matches the claim that the method renders the background by sampling a layered spherical map for rays transmitted through the volume.
